$comment: The canonical JSON encoding of an OPC UA value, per data type — the `value` field of contract/tools.json -> resultShapes.historyRecords. Both servers must produce `expected` for the same reading, so this file is the shared expectation: tests/unit/test_records.py and packages/server-node/test/unit.test.mjs each build the native value for every case name below and assert the result matches. Neither suite may skip a case, so adding one here forces both runtimes to handle it. Encodings follow OPC UA Part 6's JSON encoding where it defines one (base64 for ByteString, ISO-8601 for DateTime, a JSON string for 64-bit integers that cannot survive as a JSON number).

cases.name: boolean
cases.note: Booleans stay booleans; they must never arrive as 1/0 or "True".

cases.name: int64_small
cases.note: node-opcua carries Int64 as a [high, low] pair of 32-bit halves; python-opcua as a plain int. Both must land on the same JSON number.

cases.name: int64_negative
cases.note: The [high, low] pair is two's complement: -5 is [4294967295, 4294967291].

cases.name: int64_beyond_double
cases.note: 2^53+1. A JSON *number* loses digits here in any JS parser, so both servers switch to a decimal string at the same threshold rather than one of them silently rounding.

cases.name: double_nan
cases.note: JSON has no NaN. Emitting a bare NaN produces output that strict parsers reject, so it becomes a string.

cases.name: datetime
cases.note: A pattern, not a literal: node-opcua's Date holds milliseconds while python-opcua decodes the full microsecond resolution, and truncating Python would discard real data to match a JS limitation. This is the one permitted difference, and it is the same one the `timestamp` field carries.

cases.name: guid
cases.note: Lower-case, the RFC 4122 canonical form. node-opcua renders GUIDs upper-case.

cases.name: bytestring
cases.note: base64 of b"abc". python-opcua supplies bytes and node-opcua a Buffer; without an explicit rule these became "b'abc'" and [97, 98, 99] respectively.

cases.name: nodeid_namespace_zero
cases.note: The namespace is always spelled out, including when it is 0. python-opcua omits it ("i=2253") and node-opcua does not, which the event tools surfaced: every EventType and most SourceNodes live in namespace 0.

cases.name: statuscode
cases.note: The name alone, matching the record's own `status` field.

cases.name: localizedtext
cases.note: The text only. The locale is dropped: it is not part of the reading.

cases.name: byte_array
cases.note: An array of Byte is an array of numbers — unlike a ByteString, which is one opaque blob.

cases.name: int64_array
cases.note: Element-wise, so one oversized element does not stringify the rest.

cases.name: null
cases.note: No value at all — an aggregate interval the server holds no data for.
